production.note: US model years. First: MBUSA's '2018 Mercedes-AMG GT R Coupe Specifications' and its pricing release for 'the 2018 AMG GT R Coupe', 'Arriving in U.S. dealers this summer' (mbusa-gt-r-msrp-2017). MBUSA also published 2019 and 2020 GT R specification sheets (mbusa-2019-gt-r-specs, mbusa-2020-gt-r-specs). Last: Motor Authority, 23 December 2020, headline 'Mercedes-Benz AMG GT R dropped for 2021': the GT Black Series was added for 2021 'at the cost of the slightly tamer GT R variant, at least here in the United States'; 'First launched for 2018' (motorauthority-gt-r-dropped-2021). The GT R Pro and the 2020 GT R Roadster are not part of this record.

body.note: 'Two-door, two passenger coupe'. The AMG GT R Roadster, a limited run sold for 2020 only under its own name, is not part of this record.

fuel.note: Inferred from the spec sheet's description of the V8 biturbo petrol engine.

transmission.note: 'Transmission Type | AMG 7-Speed DCT Dual-Clutch' (AMG SPEEDSHIFT DCT transaxle)

powerHp.note: Quote: "Horsepower @ rpm | 577 @ 6,250". Also MBUSA's pricing release (mbusa-gt-r-msrp-2017): "handcrafted AMG 4.0L V8 biturbo engine rated at 577 hp". The 2019 and 2020 MBUSA spec sheets give the same 577 @ 6,250.

weightLb.note: US curb weight, coupe with the only transmission (7-speed DCT). Quote: "Curb Weight (lbs) | 3,594". The 2019 MBUSA sheet reads "Curb Weight (lbs) | 3,594 est." and the 2020 sheet "TBA". See discrepancies for the 3,428 lb Euro-spec figure.

sources.title: 2020 Mercedes-AMG GT R and GT R PRO Coupe Specifications
Mercedes-Benz AMG GT R dropped for 2021

discrepancies.reason: Market and measurement basis. MBUSA's April 2017 pricing release lists "Weight: 3,428 lbs (Euro spec; US spec may vary)", a European figure published before US data existed; the US specification sheet gives a US curb weight of 3,594 lb.
discrepancies.resolution: Use 3,594 lb, the US curb weight on MBUSA's 2018 GT R specification sheet. The 3,428 lb figure is expressly a Euro-spec number.
